newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins firm after unfreeze news.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins firm after unfreeze news.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds firmed in late trade after the news some bonds had been unfrozen and on active London bank buying, dealers said.
Russian officials have released some frozen MinFin bonds following an order from Prosecutor-General Yuri Skuratov to review all cases of freezing, Itar-Tass news agency said.
No details were available but in one particular case bonds for $21 million face value had been unfrozen out of the total $74 million.
"After the news buying became more active, especially in the fourth tranche," an International Moscow Bank dealer said.
But he added it could be a coincidence as a London bank has been bidding on an apparent client order.

Dealers said the release was generally positive for the market, otherwise weak earlier today as investors were mainly cautious ahead of Russia's Eurobond issue. The Eurobond roadshow is ending today in New York.
"Some banks were (earlier) taking profits to correct positions ahead of the issue. Investors' attitude is not quite clear at the moment," Mosbiznesbank dealer Igor Potapov said.
